purpose.description: Your code implements the required CSS changes from the task list and the HTML structure shows the described elements (image, description, cook-time, ingredients, preparation steps, and external link). The page should render with the intended styling when linked to style.css and opened in a browser.

The general objective of styling a recipe page with CSS selectors is addressed, and the project tasks are reflected in the CSS choices (image size, description font, cook-time weight, list bullets, time text color, link color, and font-family).

readability.description: The CSS rules are straightforward and easy to follow, with semantic selectors like #cook-time, .description, and .ingredients li.
Font-family is applied globally via a single selector targeting h1, h2, p, and li as requested, which keeps styles centralized.

performance.description: Code uses simple, focused selectors that are unlikely to cause specificity conflicts or unnecessary reflow.
No extraneous selectors or redundant rules; however, ensure the universal font-family rule truly targets all intended text as per the task (see note below).
